title: ZEAL – A Framework for Zero-Shot Enhanced Analysis and Learning for SEM Image Defect Correction in ICs
content: Semiconductor manufacturing encompasses a variety of precision-oriented processes, including deep ultraviolet (DUV) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, plasma etching, atomic layer deposition (ALD), and chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), all essential for producing high-density integrated circuits (ICs). As the dimensions of transistors continue to decrease, defects like line-edge roughness (LER), micro-voids, metal bridging, and pattern collapse become progressively harder to identify and correct, adversely affecting yield and reliability. Conventional optical inspection and rule-based defect classification systems, while proficient in detecting larger anomalies, often struggle to identify subtle process-induced defects at advanced technology nodes due to limitations in resolution and variations in processes [1]. Even though supervised deep learning models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs), have shown remarkable accuracy in classifying defects, their dependency on extensive labeled datasets poses a considerable challenge, especially for new defect modes in state-of-the-art semiconductor processes.
